glosses: To detach (an artillery piece) from its limber to deploy for firing.

examples.text: The gun he drove had been unlimbered near Horsell, in order to command the sand-pits, and its arrival had precipitated the action.

glosses: To clumsily put into employ (a large weapon or object).
To unsling (something, as a backpack, carried on the body with a strap); to bring (something carried) into the hands for use.
To stretch (limbs, muscles, etc., that have been cramped or unused for some time).

examples.text: "I fancy," said Psmith, "that this is one of those moments when it is necessary for me to unlimber my Sherlock Holmes system. […] Do you follow me, Comrade Maloney?" / "That's right," said Billy Windsor. "Of course." / "Elementary, my dear Watson, elementary," murmured Psmith.
Bony jumped down and unlimbered his cramped muscles before going after his camels.

examples.text: To test the possibility that her husband’s luck was indestructible, Mary went to the crap tables and made a small bet.
